title: Define the Business
description: The foundation of an exitable company is a business identity that exists independently of its founder. Right now, most solo founders describe what they do in terms of themselves — 'I am a...' An investor or acquirer needs to see a company, not a person. This step reframes your identity from operator to owner.
designMoveExample: We are a premium executive portrait studio for founders, leadership teams, and companies.
howToDoItExample:
Rewrite your homepage headline to describe the company, not yourself
Replace 'I' with 'we' across your website and pitch materials
Create a company name and brand identity separate from your personal name
Update LinkedIn to position yourself as founder/CEO of [Company], not as a freelancer
Write a one-paragraph company description in third person
exitImpact: From person → company | ❌ Not sellable yet

title: Clarify the Customer
description: Exitable businesses serve repeatable customer segments, not random individuals. Right now you're probably taking whoever comes. An acquirer needs to see a defined, reachable, repeatable customer — ideally a B2B buyer who has ongoing needs for your service.
designMoveExample: We serve HR teams, PR agencies, and executive search firms with recurring visual content needs.
howToDoItExample:
Define your ideal B2B client segment in one paragraph
Audit your current client list and identify who could become repeat buyers
Create a one-page B2B client profile
Reach out to 5 HR or PR agencies with a tailored proposition
Stop quoting for anyone outside your defined segment
exitImpact: From occasional → repeat buyers | ⚠️ More stable demand

title: Productize the Offer
description: A custom service cannot be sold — it's too dependent on negotiation, founder judgment, and bespoke delivery. An exitable business sells defined products with known inputs, outputs, and prices. Productizing means the client knows exactly what they're buying before they talk to you.
designMoveExample: Three fixed packages: Founder Day (€3K), Team Package (€6K), Content Kit (€10K).
howToDoItExample:
Design 3 fixed packages with clear deliverables and prices
Remove custom quoting from your website
Test your pricing with 5 existing clients before publishing
Create a one-page package sheet you can send to any enquiry
Practice saying 'we don't do custom' to new enquiries

title: Build Delivery Systems
description: A business that runs on founder memory and improvisation cannot be transferred. Delivery systems — SOPs, templates, checklists, tools — make your business teachable, repeatable, and eventually replaceable. Without them, you don't have a business, you have a skill.
designMoveExample: Every project follows the same SOP: brief template, shoot checklist, edit preset, delivery system.
howToDoItExample:
Document your shoot checklist step-by-step — from gear pack to wrap
Write a client brief template that works without a phone call
Package your editing presets as documented, transferable IP
Create a delivery protocol: folder structure, file naming, handoff process
Test: could a competent professional follow your SOP without you present?

title: Clarify Founder's Role
description: Every hour you spend executing is an hour not spent building. Founders who are also the primary delivery mechanism become the ceiling of their own business. This step forces clarity on what only you should do versus what the business should do — and begins separating the two.
designMoveExample: Founder = creative director and sales lead. All execution handled by team and systems.
howToDoItExample:
List every task you did last week and mark which only you can do
Move one recurring execution task off your plate this month
Write your own role description as if you were hiring a founder
Block 4 hours/week for business development only — protect it
Track how your time splits between execution vs building each week
exitImpact: From operator → builder | ⚠️ Reduces key-man risk

title: Add Team Capacity
description: You cannot scale a business you're the only person in. Adding team capacity — even one trained person — multiplies your throughput, proves the business is teachable, and removes the hard ceiling on revenue. This is where the business starts to feel real.
designMoveExample: A team of 3+ photographers and editors delivers under the brand with full quality control.
howToDoItExample:
Write the job description for your first hire this week
Identify one person you could trial on a low-stakes project
Create a quality benchmark: 10 examples of 'this is what we deliver'
Design a simple training and QA process before they start
Book a project and let them deliver it — you review only
exitImpact: From capacity ceiling → scalable delivery | ✅ Capacity scales

title: Create Recurring Revenue
description: One-off projects create one-off revenue. Exitable businesses have predictable, recurring income — because acquirers value certainty. A recurring revenue base doesn't just improve cash flow, it changes your valuation multiple entirely.
designMoveExample: 40% of revenue is recurring through annual retainers at €12K/year per client.
howToDoItExample:
Identify 5 existing clients who could benefit from quarterly content
Design a simple retainer offer with 3 tiers
Price the retainer to reward commitment — not punish the client
Send a retainer proposal to 3 clients this month
Build a dashboard tracking % recurring vs one-off revenue

title: Build Transferable Assets
description: If your business disappeared tomorrow, what would remain? A sellable business has assets that exist independently of the founder: a brand, a client database, documented IP, contracts, systems. This step inventories what you have and identifies what needs to be formalized.
designMoveExample: Transferable assets: brand, 100+ client contracts, proprietary workflow system, Lightroom IP.
howToDoItExample:
Build a CRM — even a spreadsheet is a start
Trademark your studio name and core brand assets
Formalize your Lightroom presets as documented, named IP
Get signed contracts and NDAs from all active clients
Create a one-page asset inventory: what we own, where it lives

title: Reduce Founder Dependency
description: The defining test of an exitable business: can it operate without you? Right now your clients probably want you specifically. This step measures your key-person risk and identifies what changes are needed to transfer client trust from you to the brand.
designMoveExample: Over 70% of projects delivered without founder involvement. Clients trust the brand.
howToDoItExample:
Introduce your top 10 clients to a team member — by name, in writing
Replace your name on client emails with studio branding
Have a team member lead one full client project from brief to delivery
Measure: what % of projects complete without you this month?
Credit the studio publicly — not yourself — for every win

title: Show Market Expansion
description: A local service business has limited value. An investor or acquirer needs to see a path to a larger market — regional, national, or beyond. This step establishes where you are geographically today and maps out how the business could credibly expand.
designMoveExample: Regional executive branding studio operating across CEE — Romania, Poland, Hungary.
howToDoItExample:
List 3 target markets with similar corporate density to yours
Research one potential local partner per market (agency, co-working, recruiter)
Create a market entry one-pager: TAM, target clients, entry strategy
Run one paid campaign in a new city and measure response
Make first contact with one potential regional partner this month

title: Build a Scalable Layer
description: Pure service businesses have a revenue ceiling — you can only deliver so much with people. Adding a scalable layer (software, platform, or productized IP) breaks that ceiling and dramatically changes your valuation multiple from service company to tech-enabled business.
designMoveExample: Platform layer: client portal for booking, brief management, and AI-assisted content delivery.
howToDoItExample:
Map the 3 biggest manual bottlenecks in your current delivery process
Identify one off-the-shelf tool that could replace each bottleneck
Scope a simple client portal MVP: booking + brief + delivery
Find a technical partner or agency to build it
Test with 5 clients before full rollout

title: Define the Exit Scenario
description: Most founders never think concretely about exit — they assume it happens 'eventually'. But building a business that's sellable requires knowing who would buy it, at what valuation, and what needs to be true to get there. This step builds your exit thesis.
designMoveExample: Exit target: acquisition by PR agency or HR tech platform at 1–3x revenue within 5 years.
howToDoItExample:
Research 5 companies who could realistically acquire you
Write a one-paragraph acquisition story for each buyer type
Identify what your business needs to look like for each buyer
Set a revenue and structure milestone that triggers exit readiness
Begin relationship-building with one potential acquirer now
exitImpact: From self-employment → asset sale | 🎯 Fully exitable

title: Choose Your Investors
description: Not all capital is equal. The right investor brings more than money — they bring networks, distribution, and credibility. The wrong investor creates pressure without value. This step clarifies what you actually need and what the ideal funding partner looks like.
designMoveExample: Strategic investors from media, HR, or content distribution networks as growth partners.
howToDoItExample:
List 10 investor types whose portfolio companies would benefit from your service
Research 3 CEE-based family offices or angels active in creative/tech
Write a one-paragraph investment thesis for your business
Define what 'smart money' means for your specific growth path
Attend one investor or founder event in the next 30 days
exitImpact: From funding → partnership | ✅ Better exit odds

title: Build AI Defensibility
description: AI is commoditizing the bottom of most creative markets. The question isn't whether AI affects your business — it's whether your business sits above the commoditization line. This step defines what makes you defensible and how to reinforce that position.
designMoveExample: Premium brand + proprietary system + relationships = defensible against AI commoditization.
howToDoItExample:
Audit your offer: which parts could AI replace in 3 years?
Double down on what AI can't replicate: relationships, direction, consistency
Move pricing upmarket — make your premium positioning explicit
Integrate AI tools into your workflow to stay ahead (editing, brief automation)
Write your moat statement — one sentence for your pitch deck

title: Long-term Performance Check
description: A business built to exit needs to be built to last. KPI-driven management — tracking LTV, CAC, margin, and retention — tells investors your business is run with intention, not intuition. This step benchmarks where you are and where a healthy version of this business sits.
designMoveExample: KPI dashboard: 70%+ retention, 50%+ margin, 20%+ annual growth, LTV tracked per segment.
howToDoItExample:
Calculate your current gross margin per project type
Build a simple retention tracking spreadsheet — even in Excel
Define LTV for your top 3 client segments
Set quarterly targets for your 4 core KPIs
Review metrics monthly — the number is a signal, not a judgment

title: Make the Ask
description: An investment ask is the culmination of every previous step. It requires knowing exactly how much you need, what you'll use it for, and what milestone you're funding toward. Vague asks signal that the business isn't ready. A precise ask signals a founder who knows what they're doing.
designMoveExample: Raising €1M to expand regionally, build platform layer, and reach €1M ARR by 2027.
howToDoItExample:
Build a 12-month financial model with the capital deployed
Write a one-paragraph use-of-funds statement
Define the milestone this round funds toward — one clear sentence
Identify 10 specific investors to approach in priority order
Prepare your ask slide: amount, use, milestone, structure, return thesis
exitImpact: From project → investment case | 🚀 Scale + exit optionality
